title: Annotatio V §.II: Augustine antitheses — spiritual eat/drink; sacrament vs virtue; visible vs invisible body
pass_a_gloss: As from the Apostle’s words serm. 2: that in the Supper there is something which is spiritually eaten, spiritually drunk; and in Joh. tract. 26: that there is flesh and blood, and that there is the sacrament of flesh and blood; and from the Apostle’s words serm. 2: that the sacrament is one thing, the virtue of the sacrament another; that there is something which is taken in the sacrament, and something which is eaten and drunk by the sacrament’s own truth. In Johann. tract. 59: to eat the Lord’s bread, and to eat the Lord as bread; in Psal. 98 / Epist. to Caesar: the sacrament celebrated visibly and the Sacrament understood Spiritually. To eat the body itself, and not to eat the body itself: the itself invisibly, and not the itself visibly — Joh. tract. 26.
pass_b_english: Augustine’s antitheses (via Picherellus): something spiritually eaten and drunk; flesh and blood vs their sacrament; sacrament vs the sacrament’s virtue; what is taken in the sacrament vs what is eaten in the sacrament’s truth.
Further: eat the Lord’s bread vs eat the Lord as bread; sacrament celebrated visibly vs understood spiritually; eat the body itself vs not; invisibly vs visibly (Joh. tracts).
source_text: Ut de verbis Apost. serm. 2. esse in Cœna aliquid quod spiritualiter manducatur, spiritualiter bibitur, & in Joh. tract. 26. esse carnem & sanguinem, & esse carnis & sanguinis sacramentum, & de verbis Apostoli serm. 2. esse aliud sacramentum, aliud virtutem sacramenti, esse aliquid quod sumitur in sacramento, & esse aliquid, quod ipsâ (Sacramenti) veritate manducatur & bibitur. in Johann. tractat. 59. Panem Domini manducare, & panem Dominum manducare, in Psal. 98. visibiliter celebrari sacramentum & Spiritualiter intelligi Sacramentum Epist. ad Cæsar. Ipsum corpus manducare, & non ipsum corpus manducare: Ipsum invisibiliter, & non ipsum visibiliter, in Johan. tract. 26.
